test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Mechanic) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: Which of the following expressions is not correct for electric power?
solution:
The correct answer is __**P = I²/R**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Electric power is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed or converted.
 
• The fundamental formula for electric power is:
 
 
• **P = VI**
 
 
 
• Using Ohm's Law (**V = IR**), other valid expressions are:
 
 
• **P = I²R**
 
• **P = V²/R**
 
 
 
• **P = I²/R** is not a valid expression for electric power.
 
• Therefore, option **3** is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ohm's Law**:

 
 
• **V = IR**
 
• Relates voltage, current, and resistance.
 
 
 
• **Unit of Power**:
 
 
• The SI unit of electric power is the **watt (W)**.
 
• 1 Watt = 1 Joule per second.
 
 
 
• **Electrical Energy**:
 
 
• Energy consumed = **Power × Time**.
 
• Commercial unit of energy = **kilowatt-hour (kWh)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Valid power formulas:
 
 
• **P = VI**
 
• **P = I²R**
 
• **P = V²/R**
 
 
 
• **P = I²/R** is incorrect and commonly used as a trap option in exams.
 
• Remember: multiplying by **R** gives a correct power expression, not dividing by it.
